text: Your 9:00 call starts in twenty minutes. Brewing pour-over coffee takes five minutes of hands-on pouring, while reviewing the slide deck needs twenty uninterrupted minutes. Which plan gets the slides finished before 9:00?
choices: Review the slides right now and grab coffee after
Brew coffee first, then speed-read the slides
Review half the slides, brew coffee, then finish
explanation: Reviewing right away uses the full twenty-minute window. Brewing coffee first or halfway through breaks the twenty uninterrupted minutes required.

text: Two files sit in the team folder: “Budget_Final.xlsx” and “Budget_Final_v2.xlsx”. A sticky note says: “I fixed the typo in the numbers inside v2; the summary line stayed the same.” Which file has the corrected numbers?
choices: Budget_Final, because the summary stayed the same
Budget_Final_v2, where the numbers were fixed
Either file, since the numbers must match
explanation: The note separates the fixed numbers from the unchanged summary. Only v2 carries the corrected figures.

text: A morning demo has two rooms available. The Glass Room seats 8 people and has a projector; the Oak Room seats 12 people without a projector. Nine attendees need to see the projector, and chairs cannot be moved. What follows?
choices: The Oak Room meets both needs
The Glass Room meets both needs
Neither room meets both needs as arranged
explanation: One room lacks a seat and the other lacks a projector, so neither room satisfies both conditions without changing the setup.

text: The homework portal instantly emails a confirmation code for every uploaded essay, and that email never expires. Linh checks her inbox and spam folder and finds no code. Under these rules, what is certain?
choices: Her essay has not been recorded as uploaded
The professor already graded and rejected it
The professor has not opened her inbox yet
explanation: Every uploaded essay triggers a confirmation code. No code means the upload itself was never recorded.

text: Grandma’s pancake note says: “Two scoops of flour feed four hungry people.” Six hungry friends just rang your doorbell. Keeping her exact ratio, how much flour do you need?
choices: Two and a half scoops
Three scoops
Four scoops
explanation: Four people use two scoops, which is half a scoop per person. Six people need three scoops.

text: A delivery text reads: “Your fresh coffee beans are waiting in Smart Locker 12. The lobby desk only accepts return packages.” You want to pick up your coffee beans. Where do you go?
choices: The lobby desk
Either place works for pickups
Smart Locker 12
explanation: Pickups go to Smart Locker 12, while the lobby desk only handles returns.

text: The bakery’s free-refill chalkboard says: “Same mug, same morning, receipt in hand.” You have this morning’s receipt in your pocket, but you accidentally brought yesterday’s travel mug. Which rule did you miss?
choices: Using the mug from this morning’s order
Keeping the printed receipt
Coming back on the same morning
explanation: You have today’s receipt on the same morning, but the mug itself does not match today’s purchase.

text: The neighborhood bookshop lets you drop returned books through the brass slot 24 hours a day, while borrowing a new book requires the shopkeeper, who arrives at 2:00 p.m. You stop by at noon. What can you do right away?
choices: Borrow a new novel only
Drop off your returned book only
Both return your book and borrow a new one
explanation: The return slot is open all day, including noon, whereas borrowing has to wait until 2:00 p.m.

text: Two fathers and two sons sit down together for morning phở. Each person orders his own bowl, yet the waiter brings only three bowls and everyone has a full bowl. How does that work?
choices: One person shared his broth
The waiter miscounted the table
They are grandfather, father, and son
explanation: Three generations sit at the table: the father in the middle is both a son to the grandfather and a father to his own son.

text: Trang texts the group chat: “If the acoustic show starts after 8:00, save me a front-row chair. Before 8:00, I’m still on the metro.” The café posts a start time of 8:30. What should the group do?
choices: Save a chair for Trang
Ask the band to play at 7:45
Assume Trang is skipping tonight
explanation: An 8:30 start is after 8:00, which matches the exact condition Trang gave for saving her a chair.

text: Minh offers: “I’ll bring a sweet treat for the picnic, as long as it doesn’t need a cooler.” The host suggests either gelato cones or crispy almond biscotti. Which option fits Minh’s rule?
choices: Gelato cones, because everyone loves ice cream
Almond biscotti, because they keep at room temperature
Both treats, since both are sweet
explanation: Both are sweet, but gelato melts without a cooler while biscotti stay crisp at room temperature.

text: A friend replies to your brunch invite: “That rooftop café looks amazing! I still need to check if I’m free this Sunday.” What is actually confirmed?
choices: Your friend will definitely be there
Sunday’s table is already booked
Your friend likes the café idea, but attendance is undecided
explanation: Enthusiasm for the café is clear, but Sunday availability has not been checked, so attendance is not confirmed.

text: At dawn, a courtyard statue casts a long shadow pointing straight west. Since a shadow always falls directly away from the light source, which side is the rising sun shining from?
choices: East
West
North
explanation: A westward shadow means the light is shining from the opposite direction: east.

text: An exhibition photo shows an empty stage with a single guitar stand. The caption reads only: “Ten minutes after the encore.” Which statement sticks strictly to the facts?
choices: The crowd walked out early in boredom
The stage was empty ten minutes after the encore
The concert was canceled before it began
explanation: The photo and caption tell us what the stage looked like ten minutes after the encore, not how large the crowd was earlier.

text: An art director’s note says: “Put the festival title above the illustration, and the ticket date below the illustration.” In your draft, the date is sandwiched between the title and the illustration. What one move fixes it?
choices: Move the title below the illustration
Delete the illustration
Move the date below the illustration
explanation: The title is already on top. Moving the date below the illustration puts all three elements in the requested order.

text: Your morning reel needs 30 seconds of unbroken acoustic guitar. You have three takes lasting 20 seconds, 35 seconds, and 40 seconds. You may trim a take, but you cannot loop or splice takes together. Which is the shortest take that works?
choices: The 35-second take
The 20-second take
The 40-second take
explanation: The 20-second take is too short. Both 35 and 40 seconds can be trimmed to 30, and 35 seconds is the shorter of the two.

text: On your neighborhood map, the flower market sits due north of the library, and the bakery sits due east of the library. If you stand outside the bakery and look straight toward the flower market, which way are you facing?
choices: Southeast
Northwest
Southwest
explanation: From the bakery (east of the library) to the flower market (north of the library), you look north and west: northwest.

text: Tram A stops at the Art Museum but skips Central Station. Tram B starts at Central Station but never reaches the Art Museum. Both trams stop at River Square. Starting from Central Station, how do you ride to the Art Museum?
choices: Board Tram A at Central Station, then switch to B
Stay on Tram B the entire trip
Ride Tram B to River Square, then transfer to Tram A
explanation: Only Tram B serves Central Station. Riding it to the shared stop at River Square lets you transfer to Tram A for the Art Museum.

text: The botanical glasshouse closes its gates at 8:00 p.m. and stops admitting new visitors 30 minutes before closing. What is the latest time you can enter?
explanation: Thirty minutes before the 8:00 p.m. closing time is 7:30 p.m.

text: You step onto the platform at 10:10. The local train leaves immediately and takes 35 minutes; the express train waits until 10:20 to depart and takes 20 minutes. Assuming both run on time, which train reaches your stop first?
choices: The local, because it leaves right away
The express, arriving 5 minutes earlier
Both trains arrive at the exact same minute
explanation: The local arrives at 10:45 (10:10 + 35 min). Even with a 10-minute wait, the express arrives at 10:40 (10:20 + 20 min), five minutes ahead.

text: A desk sensor logs a “low-light” note whenever brightness in the study drops below 150 lux. A low-light note appears at 12:00 noon. What does that log entry prove on its own?
choices: The study has no windows at all
A thunderstorm is passing overhead
Brightness at the sensor was below 150 lux at noon
explanation: The sensor only measures the light level at the desk. Closed curtains, shade, or clouds could cause it, so only the lux threshold is proven.

text: A vintage wall clock loses 2 minutes every hour, while a stopped pocket watch stands still at 7:00. Over a full 24-hour day, which timepiece shows the exact right time more often?
choices: The stopped pocket watch, twice a day
The slow wall clock, every hour
Neither ever shows the right time
explanation: A stopped 12-hour watch is right twice every 24 hours (at 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m.), while a clock losing 2 minutes an hour takes 15 days to drift back to the exact time.

text: You scan an undated film photograph from your childhood on Monday morning, creating “scan_01.jpg”. What does Monday’s file creation timestamp actually tell you?
choices: The childhood photo was originally snapped on a Monday
The digital scan file was saved on Monday
The film roll was developed on Monday
explanation: A digital file timestamp records when the scan was created on your computer, not when the camera shutter clicked years ago.

text: A craft shelf displays 12 teacups. A card beside them states: “Every ceramic cup on this shelf is hand-thrown.” You count 4 ceramic cups and 8 glass cups. What is the minimum number of hand-thrown cups guaranteed by the card?
choices: All 12 cups
Zero, because the glass cups are unknown
At least 4 cups
explanation: The rule guarantees the 4 ceramic cups are hand-thrown. Some glass cups might be handmade too, so we know at least 4 are.
